description: Add first-class issue prerequisite selection to the create-issue API/dialog and replace the numeric-only backlog prerequisite editor with a reusable searchable issue picker.

tasks.title: Server: atomic create-with-prerequisites API
tasks.description: Extend IIssueGrain.CreateAsync / IssueGrain.CreateAsync with an optional int[]? prerequisiteNumbers parameter. After Issue.Create builds the aggregate but before SaveIssueAsync, reuse the same LoadIssueSummaryAsync helper that AddPrerequisiteAsync uses to validate every unique number against the selected project, reject self-reference against the newly allocated number, and fail fast with a typed PrerequisiteValidationException (reason not_found / self_reference) leaving nothing persisted. Add a PrerequisiteNumbers field to CreateIssueRequest (IssueRoutes.Dtos.cs); map it in the create route handler (IssueRoutes.Crud.cs), returning ApiResults.BadRequest naming the offending number on validation failure and the full issue read model (with prerequisiteNumbers/prerequisites/canStart/blocker already populated) via IssueQuerier on success.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /projects/{projectRef}/issues with prerequisiteNumbers:[5,7] where #5 and #7 exist creates an issue whose response.prerequisiteNumbers equals [5,7]
POST with prerequisiteNumbers omitted or [] creates an issue with no prerequisites, identical to today's behavior
POST with a nonexistent number (e.g. 99999) returns 400 naming the offending number and GET /issues/{N} for the would-be number returns 404 (no readable issue left behind)
POST with a cross-project number is rejected and no issue is created in the target project
POST whose prerequisiteNumbers contains the newly allocated number is rejected as self-reference/circular and no readable issue is created
POST with [5,5,5] stores 5 exactly once; response.prerequisiteNumbers equals [5] (idempotent dedupe)
On a successful create the response includes populated prerequisites summaries (number/title/status/health/completed), canStart, and blocker reflecting the just-applied prerequisites
POST /issues/{n}/prerequisites and DELETE /issues/{n}/prerequisites/{pn} behave exactly as before this change (frozen single-add/remove contract)

Specs/Issue/Api/IssueCreationSpecs.cs (or equivalent) extended with create-with-prerequisites success, nonexistent/cross-project rejection, self-reference rejection, duplicate collapse, no-leftover-issue-on-failure, and populated-response scenarios; all previously passing issue-creation specs remain green
dotnet build Mohist.sln succeeds with warnings-as-errors (server lint) and the server test suite passes
tasks.output: packages/server changes: IIssueGrain/CreateAsync signature, IssueGrain.CreateAsync validation+persist step, PrerequisiteValidationException, CreateIssueRequest.PrerequisiteNumbers, IssueRoutes.Crud.cs mapping; extended Specs/Issue/Api/IssueCreationSpecs.cs
tasks.notes: Per design D1/D2/D3: perform validation inside the grain before the single SaveIssueAsync so atomicity is structural, not compensatory. Reuse LoadIssueSummaryAsync verbatim so create-time and edit-time existence semantics cannot diverge. The IssueCounterGrain burns the allocated slot on failure; this is established counter semantics (documented in design Risks) and requires no mitigation.

tasks.title: Web: reusable IssuePrerequisitePicker feature component
tasks.description: Introduce a new FSD feature slice at packages/web/src/features/prerequisite-picker/ exposing a single IssuePrerequisitePicker component consumed by both the create-issue dialog and the backlog editor. Props: projectId, excludeNumbers, selected (controlled), mode ('buffer' | 'live'), onAdd, onRemove, renderChips (default true). Candidate source is the existing getIssues({ projectId }) query already used by the board; filter client-side by number substring (String(number) includes term) and case-insensitive title includes; render each candidate as '#number · title · status' plus the completed/health badge from IssuePrerequisiteSummary when available. Apply excludeNumbers (current issue + already-selected) and rely on the project-scoped query to structurally exclude cross-project issues. Render selected numbers as removable chips (buffer mode mutates local state via onRemove; live mode invokes onRemove/onAdd). Render a per-prerequisite incomplete indicator when prereq.completed === false and a section-boundary summary line for canStart/blocker when supplied, reusing the existing start-readiness read model.
acceptanceCriteria: Typing a number (e.g. '42') surfaces the matching issue as a candidate showing number, title, and status
Typing a title fragment (e.g. 'auth') surfaces all issues whose titles case-insensitively contain it
The current issue (in excludeNumbers) and already-selected prerequisites are not offered as candidates
Cross-project issues are not offered because the candidate query is project-scoped
Selected numbers render as removable chips; removing a chip in mode='buffer' updates local state, in mode='live' it calls onRemove, and selecting a candidate in mode='live' calls onAdd
An incomplete prerequisite (completed === false) is flagged with an indicator, and a canStart/blocker summary line renders when those fields are supplied
Component tests cover search-by-number, search-by-title, exclusions, candidate status display, chip add/remove for both buffer and live modes, and incomplete/start-eligibility messaging
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes and npm run test:run -w packages/web is green
tasks.output: packages/web/src/features/prerequisite-picker/ slice (IssuePrerequisitePicker component + index public API + component tests)
tasks.notes: Per design D4/D7: place the component in features/ (not entities/) because it composes the entities/issue list query with selection state, keeping FSD dependency direction clean (create-issue feature and issue-detail page both import downward into this sibling feature, which imports downward into entities/issue). The mode prop is the only seam between the create dialog's buffered semantics and the backlog editor's live add/remove contract.

tasks.title: Web: New Issue dialog prerequisite selection + createIssue client
tasks.description: Extend entities/issue/api/client.ts createIssue to accept an optional prerequisiteNumbers?: number[] and forward it in the request body (the existing body spread already passes the key through). In CreateIssueDialog.tsx add a useState<number[]> prerequisite buffer, render <IssuePrerequisitePicker mode='buffer' selected={buffer} excludeNumbers={buffer} onAdd={n => setBuffer(prev => [...prev, n])} onRemove={n => setBuffer(prev => prev.filter(x => x !== n))} /> as an optional Prerequisites field, include prerequisiteNumbers on submit when non-empty, and clear the buffer in resetAndClose alongside the other fields.
acceptanceCriteria: createIssue sends prerequisiteNumbers in the request body when the caller provides it
Selecting #5 and #7 in the New Issue dialog renders both as removable chips and submit sends prerequisiteNumbers:[5,7]
Removing the #5 chip drops it from the buffer so submit then sends only [7]
Submitting with no prerequisites selected omits (or sends an empty) prerequisiteNumbers and creates an issue with no prerequisites
After a successful create and dialog close the prerequisite buffer is cleared, so reopening starts with no selections
Tests cover selection, chip removal, reset-on-close, and submit-with-and-without-prerequisites; the create-issue mutation's onSuccess still reads data.number off the unchanged read-model shape
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes and npm run test:run -w packages/web is green
tasks.output: packages/web/src/entities/issue/api/client.ts (createIssue prerequisiteNumbers) and packages/web/src/features/create-issue/ui/CreateIssueDialog.tsx (buffer state + picker + reset); updated dialog tests
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 for the server-side prerequisiteNumbers field on CreateIssueRequest and on T-002 for the picker component. Per design D5: buffer selections client-side; only send prerequisiteNumbers when non-empty to keep the no-prerequisite path byte-identical to today.

tasks.title: Web: backlog IssueConfigurationCard adopts the picker (live mode)
tasks.description: In pages/issue-detail/ui/cards/IssueConfigurationCard.tsx remove the numeric Input + Add button + handleAdd/prereqError block and the existing chip-removal block, and render <IssuePrerequisitePicker mode='live' selected={issue.prerequisites.map(p => p.number)} excludeNumbers={[issue.number, ...issue.prerequisites.map(p => p.number)]} onAdd={(n) => addPrerequisiteMutation.mutateAsync(n)} onRemove={(n) => removePrerequisiteMutation.mutateAsync(n)} />. The existing addPrerequisite/removePrerequisite clients (POST /issues/{n}/prerequisites and DELETE /issues/{n}/prerequisites/{pn}) are passed through unchanged; server validation errors surface through the picker's error rendering.
acceptanceCriteria: The bare numeric Issue # input and Add button are replaced by the searchable picker; the user is no longer required to type a raw issue number from memory
Selecting a candidate issues POST /issues/{n}/prerequisites with { prerequisiteNumber } via the existing client and, on success, the prerequisite appears on the issue
Removing a chip issues DELETE /issues/{n}/prerequisites/{pn} via the existing client and the prerequisite is removed
Server validation errors (nonexistent issue, self-reference, circular) are surfaced as readable messages instead of being silently swallowed
Start buttons and board cards continue to reflect waiting prerequisites via the existing canStart/blocker read model (no readiness-model change)
Tests cover add-via-picker, remove-via-chip, error surfacing, and the no-regression scenarios (validation errors still surface; start eligibility unchanged)
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes and npm run test:run -w packages/web is green
tasks.output: packages/web/src/pages/issue-detail/ui/cards/IssueConfigurationCard.tsx (picker swap, numeric input removed); updated backlog-editor tests
tasks.notes: Per design D6: this is a pure UI change layered over the frozen single-add/remove HTTP contract. No new add/remove endpoint is introduced. The picker's own chips subsume the legacy chip-removal block. Server-side validation behavior is identical to the numeric editor; only the selection UX changes.
